candidate: Repair operator for failed or crashed candidates
what: When a proposed change crashes or produces an invalid result, give the same session type one bounded repair attempt (depth limit) before reverting, with the traceback in the prompt.
problem_here: Brief does not say that a crash gets a repair attempt; a crash probably wastes an iteration and counts toward the decline/limit budget.
mechanism: Harness code detects crash or invalid metric, starts one more headless session in the same worktree with the error text, counts it against the limits, then keeps or reverts as usual.
evidence: Round 2 (2026-11-12): in the kit's nine recorded campaigns 0 of 56 iterations ended as crash, invalid, agent error, no change or duplicate, so there is nothing to replay a repair step on. Before round 2: AIDE aideml agent.py (pushed 2026-10-16): debug_prob and max_debug_depth; AIRA-dojo (arXiv 2507.02554, repo pushed 2026-04-14): debug limit 10 nodes or 12 h; MLEvolve debug_agent (2026-10-16); RD-Agent coder_max_loop 10, runner_max_loop 3 (docs read 2026-11-12). No ablation isolating debug was found; only code-level presence.
maturity: Present in four systems; benefit not measured separately.
cost: Small: one extra session per crash, bounded by existing limits.
simpler_alternative: Reject the iteration and let the history show the crash to the next session.
reason: Shared by four strong systems and cheap, but no measured gain; the cost of an extra session must be weighed against a fresh proposal.
cheap_local_trial: Campaigns on a harder task whose records show crashes, with and without one repair session per crash, at the same limits. Not run: no recorded crash to test on, and live campaigns cost agent usage.

what: An operator that asks a session to combine two previously kept or near-miss changes into one candidate, scored by the usual panel.
problem_here: Search is greedy on one branch; near-miss changes that were discarded are never combined with later winners.
mechanism: Harness stores discarded-but-promising diffs (first-seed gain, not confirmed); a periodic iteration gives the session two diffs to merge; same acceptance rule.
evidence: AIRA-dojo arXiv 2507.02554 (read 2026-11-12): AIRA operators (adds crossover, changes memory scoping) greedy 45.5% vs AIDE operators 39.8% on MLE-bench Lite, same policy; gain not attributed to crossover alone. MLEvolve fusion/aggregation agents, no ablation in README.
cost: Medium: needs a store of near-misses and one extra iteration type.
simpler_alternative: Let the next session read the history and re-propose the idea itself.
reason: Plausible but the AIRA gain bundles several changes; the decision rule needs evidence of improvement for a real use.
cheap_local_trial: Retrospective: take existing journals, find pairs of discarded and kept changes that touch different files, test whether the combination beats each on the panel on the char-LM benchmark.

candidate: Tree, graph or MCTS search instead of one greedy branch
what: Keep several branches and pick the parent by UCT or similar.
problem_here: Greedy on one branch can stall on a local optimum.
mechanism: Harness keeps nodes with scores; a selector chooses the parent; worktrees per branch.
evidence: AIRA-dojo (arXiv 2507.02554): MCTS/evolutionary add about 2.2 gold points with o3, policy ablation with AIDE operators marginal; Apple/EPFL arXiv 2609.40303 (earlier note): no significant difference among Chain, Greedy, UCB1, Best-of-N. MLEvolve MCGS 65.3 +/- 0.8 SEM, no ablation.
maturity: Common but unproven; reported gains within noise.
cost: High: state, selection, more runs per unit of progress on one GPU.
simpler_alternative: Greedy search with branch-on-stall restart from the best commit.
reason: Best controlled evidence shows no reliable benefit, and a single small GPU cannot afford the extra evaluations.

what: After N consecutive discards, restart from the best earlier commit or switch operator (fusion/evolution) instead of continuing the same line.
problem_here: Two declines end a campaign, but a run of discards is not handled differently.
mechanism: Counter in harness code; on threshold change the prompt mode or parent.
evidence: MLEvolve engine/agent_search.py (read 2026-11-12): stagnation on a branch triggers fusion or evolution; node_selection.py has no explicit stagnation detector. pi-autoresearch (earlier note): stop after more than 20 consecutive discards or crashes. No ablation found.
simpler_alternative: Stop the campaign after N discards (a limit the user sets).
reason: Cheap but no evidence of gain; a stop rule is the safer minimum.
cheap_local_trial: Simulate on past journals: how many campaigns had long discard streaks followed by a later keep.

what: Store plan, diff, outcome and label per iteration across campaigns and retrieve similar ones (BM25 or embeddings) for the next session.
problem_here: The next session reads only a short history of the current campaign.
mechanism: Stdlib BM25 over the journal; top-k records inserted in the prompt.
evidence: MLEvolve README (read 2026-11-12): global memory, BM25 + FAISS, no ablation. AIRA-dojo arXiv 2507.02554: memory ablation on AIDE gives nearly identical medal rates. AIBuildAI README: memorize command, no numbers. Stateless agents with harness-owned state matched baselines with 84% fewer tokens (arXiv 2610.07625, earlier note).
cost: Medium; retrieved text may bias the session.
simpler_alternative: Keep the short history and add a one-page campaign summary written by harness code.
reason: Only controlled evidence says memory does little; the BM25 variant needs no package but needs a test.
cheap_local_trial: A/B two campaigns on the char-LM benchmark with and without retrieved records, same budget, 3 repeats; compare kept gains and tokens.

candidate: Concurrent candidate/seed evaluation on several GPUs
what: Run the seed panel (or several candidates) concurrently on multiple GPUs or remote jobs.
problem_here: Wall-clock per iteration is panel size times run time unless runs are concurrent (not stated in the brief).
mechanism: Launch panel seeds as detached runs on separate devices; harness waits and then applies the rule.
evidence: SkyPilot scaling post (2026-03-18, earlier note): 16 GPUs reached the same loss about 9x faster than a simulated sequential run, no noise estimate; AIRA-dojo Slurm job arrays; MLEvolve parallel slots; RD-Agent ParallelMultiTraceExpGen.
maturity: Mature in principle; the harness already has remote runs.
cost: Money and scheduling; spending cap exists.
simpler_alternative: Shorter runs or fewer seeds with early discard.
reason: Real wall-clock gain, acceptance quality unchanged; needs extra GPUs or remote money.
cheap_local_trial: Run the 3-seed panel concurrently on one machine with two processes and check that paired results match the sequential ones.

candidate: Static check of the proposed diff before training
what: A cheap review step (diff scan for reads of validation paths, hard-coded outputs, evaluator access) before spending GPU time.
problem_here: Tampering is detected from the transcript and checksums after the session; bad diffs still cost a training panel.
mechanism: Harness code greps the diff against rules; optionally a second session reviews it.
evidence: MLEvolve code_review_agent and data_leakage_agent exist in the repository tree (read 2026-11-12), no measured effect; LLM monitors catch 42-89% (ImpossibleBench, earlier note), so rules cannot replace structure.
cost: Small for rules, a session for the reviewer.
simpler_alternative: Existing checksums and the transcript scan.
reason: Cheap tripwire; the evidence says it is not a defence on its own.
cheap_local_trial: Plant ten leaky and ten clean diffs, measure rule catch rate and false alarms.

candidate: Confirm the top two candidates, not only the last kept commit
what: Keep the runner-up kept commit and confirm both on fresh seeds before the final test.
problem_here: Greedy chain yields a single final commit; selection on noisy validation may pick a worse one.
mechanism: Harness records each kept commit's panel mean; final confirmation retrains the best two.
evidence: AIRA-dojo arXiv 2507.02554 (read 2026-11-12): top 3 validation-ranked submissions add about 10%; validation selection closes more than 60% of the validation-test gap for greedy agents. Different task (Kaggle submissions, not training repos).
maturity: Evidence from benchmark, not from this kind of harness.
cost: One more retraining of n seeds.
simpler_alternative: Existing confirmation of start vs kept commit.
reason: The harness already confirms; extra gain is unshown for its setting.
cheap_local_trial: Replay journals: how often the best-by-panel commit differs from the best-by-confirmation commit.

what: Streamlit or Flask UI over run logs and traces.
problem_here: Only status, watch and curve in the terminal.
maturity: Mature but tied to its log format.
simpler_alternative: Static HTML report from the metrics file using the standard library.
reason: No evidence that it improves results, validity, cost or reliability.

what: Use upstream autoresearch as the loop.
mechanism: Instruction-only rules; agent edits train.py, parses log, runs git.
evidence: Earlier note (primary read 10-11 Nov 2026) and API check 2026-11-12: pushed 2026-03-26, README MIT but no LICENSE file; budget, evaluation call and seed in agent-editable train.py; one measurement per change.
cost: Loses guard, seed panel, test seal.
reason: Weaker on every validity row; useful only as a pattern.

what: Use AIDE as the proposer/search layer.
problem_here: Would replace the proposer, not the harness.
mechanism: Draft/debug/improve tree; LLM extracts the metric from output.
evidence: agent.py and README read 2026-11-12 (MIT, pushed 2026-10-16, 1,620 stars); no frozen evaluator; step limit only.
cost: Loses harness scoring unless the metric reviewer is bypassed.
reason: Could replace nothing without weakening scoring; operators can be borrowed.

what: Research framework with swappable policies and operators.
problem_here: Would be a research platform alongside the harness.
mechanism: Greedy, MCTS, evolutionary with operators on Slurm.
evidence: README and arXiv 2507.02554 read 2026-11-12: CC BY-NC 4.0, pushed 2026-04-14, 20 seeds full benchmark 31.6 +/- 0.8.
simpler_alternative: Read the paper's operator prompts only.
reason: Licence and Kaggle focus; its value is the ablations, which are already used.

what: MCGS search with memory, fusion and code review for Kaggle-style tasks.
problem_here: Could replace the proposal/search layer only.
mechanism: Subprocess execution, metric printed by candidate code.
evidence: Repository files read 2026-11-12 (Apache-2.0, pushed 2026-10-16, 471 stars); leaderboard 61.33 +/- 1.33; no sandbox, no held-out check in code, no ablation.
reason: Strong benchmark rate, but weaker on validity and unproven by ablation.

what: Microsoft research-and-development agent with Docker and UI.
evidence: README and docs read 2026-11-12 (MIT, 15,342 stars, pushed 2026-10-21); 30.22 +/- 1.5 on MLE-bench with 6 seeds.
reason: Not a drop-in for an existing training repo; lower medal rate than newer systems.

what: Agent that builds models from a task description (manager + designer, coder, tuner).
problem_here: Different job: build a model from scratch.
mechanism: Agent loop with candidates and cross-run memory; backends Claude, OpenAI, DeepSeek.
evidence: README and arXiv 2604.14455 abstract read 2026-11-12 (MIT, pushed 2026-11-11); leaderboard 63.11 +/- 0.44; 70.7% self-reported; no seeds or ablations stated.
cost: Model subscription; selection and anti-cheating not stated.
reason: Cannot replace the harness or a part of it: validity controls not stated.
